newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Graboplast buys wooden floor tile maker.
newsitem.headline: Graboplast buys wooden floor tile maker.

text.p: Hungarian home improvement product manufacturer Graboplast said on Saturday it had purchased a majority stake in wooden floor tile maker Kecskemeti Parkettagyarto Kft.
"Graboplast has acquired an 88 percent stake in Kecskemeti Parkettagyarto Kft," Peter Jancso, Graboplast's Chairman told a news conference.
"The company's business profile completely fits with Graboplast's profile of home improvement," he said.
Jancso declined to reveal the purchase price.

Jancso said Kecskemeti Parkettagyar posted a pre-tax profit of 30 million forints on sales of 1.150 billion forints in 1996, with domestic sales accounting for around 60 percent and German-dominated west European exports the rest.

He said Graboplast would rapidly start to integrate Kecskemeti's products into its own export distribution network, and added it would raise Kecskemeti's capital by at least 300 million forints later this year.
Graboplast's 88 percent stake represents a nominal 211.2 million forints of Kecskemeti's capital of 240 million forints
"We think Kecskemeti's sales revenues will exceed 1.5 billion forints this year, and will have annual sales of above two billion forints in 12 months," Jancso said.
"We are planning to invest in one-and-a-half to two years to boost capacity and make it a significant eastern European wooden floor tile manufacturer."
Answering a question Jancso said Graboplast will make a buyout offer to other shareholders, including the local municipality of Kecskemet city.
The Graboplast group also produces PVC floor covers, artificial leather, carpets, wall-papers, tablecloth and other fine textiles.
On Friday Graboplast shares rallied to a record high of 9,300 forints before they retreated to finish at 9,000 forints, down 100.
